lines.text: Job calls his friends miserable comforters and says he would use his mouth to encourage them.
Job says God has devastated all his cities, shattered him while he was at ease, and seized him by the neck.
Job has sewn sackcloth over his skin, and he says his hands are free of violence and his prayer is pure.
Job says his witness is at the city gate, and that his friends are his scoffers.
Job says that if he looks for Sheol as his home, there is no hope for him.
